title: State, Change, Event, Transition, Behavior and Dynamics
results: State is a boundary/question-relative representation and future-relevant history compression, not complete Reality.
State, observation, estimate and recorded operational state are distinct.
State representations can be nonunique, nonminimal and hidden/unobservable.
Change is projection-relative and stuttering proves unchanged modeled state does not imply unchanged wider Reality.
Continuous dynamics falsifies a universal discrete-transition ontology.
Event is a modeled distinguished occurrence/boundary in behavior rather than a guaranteed canonical atom of Reality.
Event, transition, event record and timestamp are distinct.
Transition granularity and atomicity are abstraction-relative.
Behavior/trajectory is more general than a current state, finite lifecycle or event sequence.
Dynamics constrains possible evolution; behavior is one realized/modelled trajectory.
Dynamics may be deterministic, nondeterministic, stochastic, continuous, discrete or hybrid.
System/environment/input partition is boundary-relative and environment assumptions belong in the model contract.
Transition relation and temporal order do not by themselves prove causation.
Current Ordivon AttemptState is an operational projection, not a foundations ontology.
antiCollapses: No modeled change != no Reality change
